Even under that central case, the course's testing component — validating a design against measured behavior on real hardware, in a domain where miscalibrated trust in a simulation is a known failure mode — keeps a trained human in the verification loop, and the dampener from low verification tolerance no longer fully offsets the higher F1, allowing the rating to cross into Medium. The ABET-relevant engineering credit-hour floor persists absent accreditor-level change, but it caps rather than eliminates the erosion, since this course is not core scaffolding for the rest of the curriculum. The honest uncertainty is substantial here — RF/microwave is a specialized niche where both capability and diffusion could move faster or slower than the central case suggests.
ELE 4620.d: Students develop an understanding of Microwave and RF design principles, simulation, and testing. The emphasis will be on the "real world" use of these fundamental principles in RF, microwave, and wireless systems. Simulation is an integral part of the course since students learn to use a Finite Element simulation tool to develop a better understanding of structures and devices covered in the course.
